items.title: Winard Harper interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 10, 2014
items.q: You know Carl Allen told this anecdote about Billy Higgins.

ctx.x: the music work. I remember Higgins telling me stories about that period when he was, you know, life was really a struggle for him. He had pawned his drums and he’d come to the gig and no drums. And he’d go in the back of the Vanguard and come out with a phone book and a coat hanger or something, and still make a gig. You’d hear about guys playing a pie pan, and they could still — you know their sound is there.

You know Carl Allen told this anecdote about Billy Higgins. He was playing in a club and he says that he was just sort of not really doing it. And all of a sudden this hand came over and took over on the ride cymbal and it was Billy Higgins. And he said the whole room just like —
